newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedbank acquires 12.5 pct in Hoiupank.
newsitem.headline: Swedbank acquires 12.5 pct in Hoiupank.

text.p: Swedish banking group Swedbank said on Friday it had signed an agreement to acquire 12.5 percent of shares in Estonia's second largest bank Hoiupank.
Swedbank bought the shares from Hansapank, the current main owner in Hoiupank and Estonia's largest bank, Swedbank said in a statement.
The deal means that Swedbank will become the third largest owner in Hoiupank after the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Estonia's cental bank Eesti Pank.
Hoiupank is listed on the stock exchange in Tallinn and has a total market capitalisation of close to 600 million crowns, Swedbank said.
The bank explained its move by saying it wanted to serve its customers better.
"Estonia's economy is growing rapidly, as is the trade with Sweden and other Nordic countries," Swedbank's deputy managing director Hakan Kallaker said in a statement.
"We can see a significant increase in interest among our company customers for business opportunities in Estonia and other Baltic states."
The deal should also be seen as an expansion of the bank's Nordic strategy.
"We estimate that the Baltic region will play a more important role also in the Nordic cooperation and for companies in the Nordic countries," Kallaker said.
The share acquisition is conditional on approval by Swedish and Estonian authorities, the company said.
